issue_context.title: Convert to generated regex fixer is disabled on regex parse errors hit during counting captures
issue_context.body:
```
    private static Regex regex = new Regex(@"abc\g");
```
Run the fixer, it gets disabled with a banner, clicking on 'show stack' gives the below
```
System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexParseException : Invalid pattern '\g' at offset 2. Unrecognized escape sequence \\g.
   at System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexParser.ScanCharEscape()
   at System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexParser.ScanBasicBackslash(Boolean scanOnly)
   at System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexParser.ScanBackslash(Boolean scanOnly)
   at System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexParser.CountCaptures(RegexOptions& optionsFoundInPattern)
   at System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexParser.ParseOptionsInPattern(String pattern,RegexOptions options)
   at async System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generator.UpgradeToGeneratedRegexCodeFixer.ConvertToSourceGenerator(<Unknown Parameters>)
   at System.Runtime.ExceptionServices.ExceptionDispatchInfo.Throw()
```
Parse errors that the capture-counting path skips do not hit this, eg.,
```c#
private static Regex regex = new Regex(@".{23423423434324243}");
```
This will offer the fixer and run it. (Possibly it should not offer the fixer, but at least it doesn't crash.)

as an aside, the message `Unrecognized escape sequence \\{0}.` should be `Unrecognized escape sequence \{0}.`

review_comments: It would be better to not flag / offer a fix in this case too, but apparently it was not caught during the parse in validation and guess we cannot detect it early

I'm not sure we want to - were refactoring the code, we weren't asked to validate the pattern. We just need to parse successfully enough to get the one thing we need.
VS has other code that squiggles this pattern.

I think it's better to not offer suggestion in case the pattern was not parse able. i.e. it better to be checked in the analyzer and not flag the pattern if it was not parse able, probably in `ValidateParameters` method: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5acf49010ca41dde468bde9ce5647bdfcbe4d7ec/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/gen/UpgradeToGeneratedRegexAnalyzer.cs#L158

@buyaa-n I have fixed this. I left the catch in the fixer as well, -- I'm not sure whether there's any way for the fixer to be executed even when the analyzer does not offer it, but I see the fixer is written defensively and this is consistent with that.

I updated the unit test and also verified in VS.
